# `local-storage-escape`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: correctness · Profile: none · Default: warning · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports a view or pointer into local storage retained by a returned aggregate, a
callee, a longer-lived container, an output parameter, or direct assignment to
module state.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

The retained value aliases stack storage that is reused or expires when the
function returns. Later access can observe overwritten bytes or invalid memory.

## When it fires

A view counts the same way `returning-local-slice` connects one to its array: a
slice of it, a `bufPrint`-family or `std.mem.print` result formatted into it, or
a fixed writer's `buffered()` bytes. A file writer or reader, or a `.fixed`
writer, built over the array (`file.writer(io, &buffer)`) keeps it as its
buffer, so returning or storing one escapes the same way. The rule reports such
a view held by a returned struct or tuple, assigned to a module-level variable or through an
output parameter, or appended to or used as a key of a standard container that a
parameter or module binding declares; and the address of a local passed directly
to `append`, `insert` or `put` on a parameter or module binding. A pointer
handed to a nested call, such as the buffer of a `bufPrint` whose result the
receiver copies, is that call's input and is not reported, and neither is a
scoped push: a `defer` in the appending block, with no exit in between, that
removes the entry again (`pop`, a shrink or clear, `items.len -= n`,
`orderedRemove`/`swapRemove` of the last element, or for `put` a removal of the
same key). Copy the bytes into storage whose lifetime matches the retaining
aggregate. Calls whose summaries only borrow the argument are not reported.

It also reports the address of a `var` local, or of a runtime parameter, that a
function returns directly or inside a struct or tuple (`return &value;`,
`return .{ .ptr = &value };`): a parameter is the callee's own copy. Comptime
parameters are not storage, and a projection such as `&self.field` is left out
because through a pointer parameter it addresses the caller's memory.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
var saved: []const u8 = &.{};

fn remember() void {
    var scratch = [_]u8{ 1, 2, 3 };
    saved = scratch[0..];
}
```
